name: Pā̃ch Parganiā
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 5 other works read were silent
catalog_citation: Grierson, G. A. 1903. Linguistic Survey of India. Vol. V: Indo-Aryan Family, Eastern Group. Part II: Specimens of the Bihārī and Oṛiyā Languages. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing, India.
catalog_locator: p. 24 (general Bihārī introduction, paragraph 'As regards Accent'; archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.32104 leaf n38, page image read); Pā̃ch Parganiā section pp. 1…
catalog_quote: As regards Accent, the general rule is to throw it back as far as possible, but there are exceptions, and in such case the accent will be indicated by a ʹ on the accented vowel, as in dekhᵃláhⁱ quoted above. The accent cannot be thrown further back than the antepenultimate, and if the penultimate is long the accent falls on it. Thus, dekhalᵃkaínhⁱ, not dekhalákainhⁱ.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim on the held p. 24 page image (one example-word glyph aside). The classification (weight-sensitive (tentative), right-edge Latin-type window, 'general rule.. exceptions') follows the source faithfully, and the record already carries the honest caveat that the rule is Grierson's statement for Bihārī as a whole, not for Pā̃ch Parganiā. Every later description reachable — Dutta 2023 (held), LSI-Bihar 2020 Kurmali Thar/Magahi (downloaded now), and Grierson's own Seven Grammars 1883-87 (downloaded now) — is silent on stress, so nothing contradicts the classification, but nothing lect-specific supports it either: 'thin'. The one unconsulted candidate (Mahato 1990, Hindi, print-only) is of unknown stress content; no reclassification or grade change is warranted now. No duplicate in the catalog (no kudm1238/sadr1238 record), though outside sources sometimes treat Panchpargania as a name for Kurmali.

sources.note: Only modern linguist-authored treatment of Panchparganiya vs Sadri/Kurmali/Khortha; a contact overview, so low odds of a stress rule, but it would settle whether any prosodic difference among the four 'Sadani' lects is reported and bears on the Panchpargania/Kurmali identity question (LSI-Bihar 2020 and Wikipedia fold Panchpargania into Kurmali; Glottolog and Grierson keep them apart).
